q: How does a green hydrogen plant earn CCTS credits under BM EN01.002?
title: Green hydrogen under BM EN01.002
short: BM EN01.002 credits a new electrolyser that makes hydrogen from water using a new captive solar or wind plant, supplying an existing user that made hydrogen from coal, gas or oil before. Grid power can be at most a tenth of the captive renewable power used, measured each year.
audience: Green hydrogen developers, refineries and ammonia plants

ul: Both the captive renewable plant and the electrolyser must be new. Retrofits and capacity additions are not covered.
The hydrogen goes to an existing dedicated consumer named in the PDD, such as an ammonia plant or refinery, which used grey hydrogen from coal gasification or steam reforming of gas or oil before.
Renewable power comes from captive solar or wind. Renewable energy certificates do not count.
Grid electricity consumed divided by captive renewable electricity consumed must stay below 0.1 each year, checked by the verifier.
The project may use no more than 5 per cent of the drinking water available locally.
A contract with the consumer must rule out double counting.
Adapted from UNFCCC CDM methodology AM0124 (version valid from 27 September 2023).
